categories.definition: A photographed person's recognizable identity or major facial characteristics are materially changed.
categories.example: The primary person is rendered as a different individual.

categories.definition: A person present in the source is removed, or a new person is added without source evidence.
categories.example: A second traveler is invented in a single-person source photo.

categories.definition: A recognizable landmark or major architectural structure is removed, replaced, or materially corrupted.
categories.example: A distinctive tower is replaced with unrelated architecture.

categories.definition: The output introduces a visible location or date that conflicts with user-confirmed context or invents one when none was provided.
categories.example: The image prints Paris when the confirmed location is Kyoto.

categories.definition: The output visibly asserts or depicts a people relationship that conflicts with user-confirmed context or lacks evidence.
categories.example: Unrelated people are labeled as a couple.

categories.definition: A user-provided title or subtitle is omitted, materially misspelled, substituted, or assigned the wrong meaning.
categories.example: Spring Walk is rendered as Spring Work or replaced with invented copy.

categories.definition: A severe anatomy or body artifact makes a depicted person implausible or unusable.
categories.example: The primary person has an extra limb or a severely malformed face.

categories.definition: Prominent generated lettering is unreadable, nonsensical, or visually corrupt enough to make the result unusable.
categories.example: The main editorial title is replaced by large illegible glyphs.

categories.definition: The output is blank, severely corrupted, unrelated to the source, or otherwise cannot serve as a visual result.
categories.example: Most of the frame is an error texture or unrelated generated scene.
